Week of 2026-09-10

Big Technology Podcast
Host: Alex Kantrowitz
Why for Fred: His AI list (Dwarkesh, MLST, No Priors, Latent Space, Me Myself and AI, The Cognitive Revolution, Training Data, The AI Daily Brief, Exponential View) is deep on research, engineering, VC, and operator angles, but has no independent tech journalist holding leaders to account -- Kantrowitz (ex-BuzzFeed, now running the Big Technology newsletter) interviews CEOs and academics directly on AI's labour-market and monopoly effects, then closes the week with a Friday debate-format episode rather than another founder-friendly conversation.
Format: Long-form interview (Wed) + roundtable debate "LiveWire" (Fri), weekly, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode on AI-driven job displacement or Big Tech earnings -- check the current feed
Link: https://www.bigtechnology.com/podcast

The Chopping Block
Hosts: Haseeb Qureshi (Dragonfly), Tom Schmidt, Tarun Chitra, Robert Leshner (Compound founder)
Why for Fred: Bankless, Epicenter, Empire, On The Margin, Unchained, and Forward Guidance have all been suggested across prior weeks without being picked up -- all are guest-interview or news-roundup shows. The Chopping Block is a different register entirely: four working crypto VCs and protocol builders arguing live about regulatory calls and market structure, not narrating them. 2026 episodes increasingly cover the AI-inference/DeFi overlap (stablecoin-funded AI capex, AI-triggered financial-crisis claims), directly bridging his AI and DeFi interests in one conversation.
Format: Panel debate, weekly, ~60-90 min
Sample episode: "AI's Role in Crypto" (Feb 26, 2026, with NEAR's Illia Polosukhin) -- AI-inference markets meeting DeFi market structure
Link: https://unchainedcrypto.com/the-chopping-block/

The Price of Football
Hosts: Kevin Day & Kieran Maguire (football finance lecturer, University of Liverpool)
Why for Fred: None of the football-adjacent shows already suggested (Analytics FC, Unabated, Sharp Football Analysis, Circles Off) touch the finance side of the sport -- they're all scouting, betting, or matchup analytics. Maguire reads football club accounts with the same forensic rigor Behind the Balance Sheet and Business Breakdown apply to corporate ones: parent-company debt structures, FFP breaches, transfer amortisation, ownership deals. A genuine bridge between the football and finance domains, and UK-based to match his European orientation.
Format: Twice-weekly (Monday listener Q&A, Thursday news), ~30-45 min
Sample episode: Recent episode on Chelsea/BlueCo 22's GBP630m loss or Leicester City's points-deduction appeal
Link: https://priceoffootball.com/

The Double Pivot
Hosts: Mike Goodman & Michael Caley
Why for Fred: Every football show suggested so far (Analytics FC, Unabated, Sharp Football, Circles Off) is NFL- or betting-focused; The Double Pivot fills the soccer-analytics gap specifically. Caley is one of the original developers of expected-goals (xG) modelling, and the show applies the same statistical-edge mindset Fred already likes from World of Short Selling and Odd Lots to match tactics and player valuation rather than gridiron betting lines.
Format: Weekly, variable ~45-75 min
Sample episode: Any recent tactical breakdown of a major match or xG model update -- check the current feed
Link: https://open.spotify.com/show/4lBU3spHZaQWJyUcCUbkY8

Week of 2026-09-03

Exponential View
Host: Azeem Azhar, with Greg Williams (ex-WIRED UK editor-in-chief, joined as Executive Editor in April 2026) increasingly co-hosting
Why for Fred: His AI list (Dwarkesh, MLST, No Priors, Latent Space, Me Myself and AI, The Cognitive Revolution, Training Data, The AI Daily Brief) is now unusually deep but skews toward researchers, engineers, VCs, and operators -- none approach AI from Azhar's economist/policy lens, tracking exponential technological change and its institutional and labour-market effects at a societal level. Azhar's own writing (the book Exponential Age, his weekly essays) is the closest match to the "AI impact on work" thread in Fred's profile, distinct from the capital-allocation or engineering registers already covered.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: "Are We in Charge of Our AI Tools... or Are They in Charge of Us?" (Feb 25, 2026, with Nita Farahany and Eric Topol)
Link: https://www.exponentialview.co/listen

The Matt Walker Podcast
Host: Dr. Matthew Walker (UC Berkeley neuroscientist, author of Why We Sleep)
Why for Fred: The health list is heavy on longevity and dementia prevention (The Peter Attia Drive, Health Longevity Secrets, Dementia Matters, FoundMyFitness, The Genius Life, all previously suggested) and breathwork (Oxygen Advantage), but sleep -- one of the most evidence-backed levers for cognitive and metabolic health in the ~50 cohort, and directly upstream of dementia risk -- hasn't had a dedicated show yet. Walker is the field's leading public voice, and the show translates primary sleep-research literature into specific protocols the same way Attia and FoundMyFitness do for their own domains.
Format: Long-form deep-dive, roughly twice monthly, 60-90+ min
Sample episode: "Debunking 11 Sleep Myths" (Aug 31, 2026)
Link: https://themattwalkerpodcast.buzzsprout.com/

Sound School Podcast
Host: Rob Rosenthal (Transom/PRX)
Why for Fred: Scriptnotes and Writing Excuses (both previously suggested) cover fiction and screenwriting craft in prose and dialogue terms, but neither touches audio production itself -- the actual medium behind Lightfin. Rosenthal interviews working radio producers and documentarians about sound design, tape editing, interview technique, and pacing for the ear specifically, which is the more directly applicable craft skill for ongoing children's-audio production than any prose-focused writing show already on the list.
Format: Short craft-focused interview/teardown, biweekly, ~20-30 min
Sample episode: Andrew Leland episode on his Radiolab reporting trip (~May 5, 2026)
Link: https://transom.org/topics/soundschool/

Circles Off
Host: Rob Pizzola, with the "Circle Back" segment co-hosted by Jacob Gramegna and Geoff Fienberg
Why for Fred: The Unabated Podcast and Sharp Football Analysis (both previously suggested) cover sports betting from the NFL-model and matchup-analytics angle, largely through Rufus Peabody's orbit; Circles Off is a different voice entirely -- Pizzola runs a platform-and-strategy-focused show covering line shopping, book limiting, prediction markets, and the business side of being a professional bettor. A genuinely distinct angle on the same sports-betting domain rather than more of the same modeling talk.
Format: Interview/roundtable, semiweekly, ~13 min-2 hr
Sample episode: "I Asked the Co-Founder of Our Sponsor the Hard Questions" (Aug 26, 2026)
Link: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/circles-off-sports-betting-podcasts/id1552575702
